Teaching R1 a Motion

Unitree R1 · MuJoCo · Motion tracking

Teaching the robot a motion, from idea to the real robot

Five stages in the actual order of work. Each stage states where it runs, what to do, which files it produces, and which condition must be met before moving on. Running example: R1 standing on one leg.

How files flow through the stages

Scriptphases + timing
→
.csvreference pose sequence, 31 values per frame
→
.npzposes + per-body velocities
→
model_xx.ptmodel during training
→
policy.onnxexported model for the C++ controller
→
Real R1Mimic mode in r1_ctrl
1

Come up with the idea and write the script

Pen and paper

Describe the motion in words and split it into phases with concrete timings.

What to do

  • Pick the teaching approach: tracking (follow a reference) for motions with a specific shape.
  • Split into phases, each at least about 1 second long.
  • Start and end in the default standing pose.
  • If it involves standing on one leg: shift the centre of mass first, then lift the leg.
  • Keep the total around 5–10 seconds for a first motion.

Example script: "stand on one leg"

TimePhase
0–1 sStand upright
1–2.5 sShift weight onto the right leg
2.5–3.5 sLift the left leg 10 cm
3.5–6.5 sHold
6.5–9 sLower the leg, shift weight back
9–10 sStand upright

Output

script
2

Create the reference motion data

PC · Python + MuJoCo · no GPU needed

Turn the script into a pose sequence for R1: each frame holds the base position, base orientation and 24 joint angles.

Four ways to create a motion

Generate with IKSet position targets (feet, centre of mass) and let Python solve the joint angles. Suits simple motions.
Film a personGVHMR extracts 3D motion, GMR retargets it to the robot's joints.
Mocap librariesAMASS, LAFAN1 (the dance1_subject2 dance comes from here).
Teleoperated demoQuest 3 + xr_teleoperate --record. Suits arm motions.

R1 CSV format (31 columns)

ColumnContents
1–3Base position x, y, z (metres)
4–7Base orientation, quaternion x, y, z, w
8–3124 joint angles (radians), in r1.xml order

30 frames per second. 10 seconds = 301 rows.

Convert CSV to NPZ

python scripts/csv_to_npz.py \
  --input-file one_leg_left.csv \
  --output-name one_leg_left.npz \
  --input-fps 30 --output-fps 50 \
  --robot r1 --render

The --robot r1 branch has to be added to the script yourself (the repo currently only has g1 and g1_23dof).

Exit condition Watch the --render video. The stance foot does not slide (under 5 mm), does not tilt and does not sink into the floor. While on one leg, the centre of mass stays inside the stance foot's support area. No joint is close to its limit.
Results from the example run: slide 0 mm · tilt 0° · lift height 101 mm · centre of mass 24 mm inside the foot edge · no joint near its limit.

Output

one_leg_left.csvone_leg_left.npz
3

Train with RL (tracking)

PC · NVIDIA GPU (RTX 3080) · a few hours

Thousands of virtual R1s practise following the reference file at once. A robot is rewarded for matching the reference and its episode is ended when it drifts too far. The robot learns to balance by itself.

One-time setup for R1

  • Edit r1.xml: in the <contact> section, change wrist_pitch_link to wrist_roll_link.
  • Copy src/tasks/tracking/config/g1/ to config/r1/.
  • Switch to the R1 model, body names *_wrist_roll_link, task name Unitree-R1-Tracking-No-State-Estimation.

Training command

python scripts/train.py \
  Unitree-R1-Tracking-No-State-Estimation \
  --motion_file=.../one_leg_left.npz \
  --env.scene.num-envs=2048

How the robot is scored

CriterionWeight
Body part positions and orientations match the reference+1.0 / +1.0
Linear and angular velocities match+1.0 / +1.0
Base (torso) matches the reference+0.5 / +0.5
Jerky motion−0.1
Joints hitting limits, limbs colliding−10
Drift from the reference over 25 cmepisode ends

Plus deliberate pushes, friction changes and centre-of-mass offsets so the model holds up better on the real robot.

Exit condition In TensorBoard: reward rises and then levels off, and episode length approaches the full motion length (the robot no longer falls or drifts off the reference).

Output

logs/rsl_rl/…/model_xx.ptpolicy.onnx + policy.onnx.data
4

Test in simulation

PC · MuJoCo · USB game controller

Two layers of testing. The second layer runs the exact C++ program used on the real robot, with the robot swapped for the simulator.

4a · View the model in mjlab

python scripts/play.py \
  Unitree-R1-Tracking-No-State-Estimation \
  --motion_file=.../one_leg_left.npz \
  --checkpoint_file=logs/rsl_rl/.../model_xx.pt

Open intermediate checkpoints too, to watch the robot improve over time.

4b · Sim2sim with the real program

# terminal 1
./simulate/build/unitree_mujoco
# terminal 2
cd deploy/robots/r1/build
./r1_ctrl --network=lo

lo means talking to the simulator on the same machine. Use the controller exactly as on the real robot.

Exit condition Completes the full motion several times in a row with no falls and no shaking. Entering and leaving Mimic mode is smooth.

Robot falls or moves oddly: go back to stage 2 (fix the reference) or stage 3 (train more).

5

Deploy to the real R1

PC ↔ R1 over LAN cable · robot remote

Add the model to the control program as a new mode (state), then run it step by step on a gantry.

Place the files and declare the mode

deploy/robots/r1/config/policy/mimic/one_leg/
├── exported/policy.onnx (+ .data)
└── params/one_leg_left.npz, deploy.yaml
Mimic_OneLeg:
  transitions: {Passive: LT + B.on_pressed}
  motion_file: config/policy/mimic/one_leg/params/one_leg_left.npz
  policy_dir:  config/policy/mimic/one_leg/
  end_state: Velocity

Add this to config.yaml, along with a button combo to enter the mode from Velocity. Then cmake .. && make.

Run on the robot

  1. Hang the robot on the gantry, power on, wait for zero-torque.
  2. Press L2 + R2 to enter debug mode (turns off the factory software).
  3. Plug in the LAN, set the PC IP to 192.168.123.222, netmask 255.255.255.0.
  4. Run ./r1_ctrl --network=enp5s0 (find the interface name with ifconfig).
  5. LT + ↑ stand up → RT + A walk → combo to enter Mimic.
  6. When the motion ends, the robot returns to Velocity by itself (end_state).
Emergency stopLT + B returns to Passive. Keep a finger on it at all times.
Use a gantryAlways hang the robot the first time, feet just touching, then lower gradually.
Self-protectionIf the robot tilts too far or loses connection, it drops to Passive by itself.

Result

R1 performs the motion

What R1 is still missing compared with G1 (per the source code, 04/2026)

  • r1.xml references a body that does not exist (*_wrist_pitch_link), so MuJoCo errors on load. Fix it before training.
  • No tracking task exists for R1 yet: create config/r1/ and add an r1 branch to csv_to_npz.py.
  • deploy/robots/r1 only has the walking mode. The Mimic mode must be copied from G1 (State_Mimic.h/.cpp) and adapted for 24 joints.
  • For a shortcut to learn the workflow: G1 already has all five stages working with the dance1_subject2 dance.

Commands, file names and weights are taken from the unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_mjlab repo (commit 13/04/2026). The R1 parts marked "add yourself" are proposals and have not been test-run on a GPU. English version of "Quy trình dạy R1 một động tác".
